description: New Zealand geography, Latin phrases, military aviation, geology, British food, volcanoes, folklore, literature, flight systems, urban history and engineering make this one of the revival’s widest-ranging stretches of general knowledge.

s06e01.description: Golf-course sequencing, breakfast cereals, screenshots, Miss Scarlett in Cluedo, fire and brimstone and Would I Lie to You? all precede a geographical trip to New Zealand’s Cook Strait.

s06e02.description: Car manufacturers, the Joker in a deck of cards, coconut shies, political landslides and the number of days in November all appear before the Queen’s famous phrase annus horribilis gives the episode its rather more elegant Latin identity.

s06e03.description: World capitals are compared by distance from London before Planet of the Apes, Bel Air, the cutting-room floor, Oktoberfest, JPEG files and Bridget Jones author Helen Fielding enter the ladder. Aviation eventually adds the B-52 Stratofortress.

s06e04.description: World rivers are arranged geographically before prawn-cocktail crisps, tug of war, moving ‘like lightning’, Hawaii’s Aloha State nickname and HB pencils all appear. Geology contributes the wonderfully named hoodoos.

s06e05.description: Dog breeds, self-checkouts complaining about unexpected items, croutons, Goths, bathroom grouting and the Bayeux Tapestry all appear before the questions head to Melton Mowbray and its famously food-heavy British identity.

s06e06.description: Cricketer Jofra Archer, Joey’s seven sisters in Friends, the original textile-worker Luddites and units of length all appear before volcanic history brings in Mount Tambora. A sitcom family tree and one of history’s largest eruptions share the same ladder.

s06e07.description: Explorers from Marco Polo to Edmund Hillary are ordered by birth before seaside rock, Comic Relief’s red nose, beaver dams and surgical scrubs appear. Folklore adds the Grim Reaper, who is at least admirably easy to recognise.

s06e08.description: Sweeney Todd’s Fleet Street, Barcelona and Catalonia, manatees as ‘sea cows’, possible opening chess moves and Watergate reporters Woodward and Bernstein all feature before The Godfather author Mario Puzo enters the quiz.

s06e09.description: Dublin’s River Liffey, the anglerfish’s lure, Theresa May’s time as Home Secretary and Millie Bobby Brown in Stranger Things all feature before aviation gets technical with a four-digit transponder code.

s06e10.description: Dubrovnik, Edward Hopper’s Nighthawks, British islands arranged north to south, a piano’s 88 keys and fortune cookies all appear before the Spitfire gives the episode its aviation landmark.

s06e11.description: Cricket equipment, The Graduate, fictional worlds from Hobbiton to Hogwarts, Amnesty International’s candle symbol and Antony Gormley’s hundred figures at Crosby Beach all appear before literature contributes the iceberg theory.

s06e12.description: Dates, bowling strikes, talking ‘nineteen to the dozen’, Siberia, the gluteus maximus and Hellmann’s mayonnaise all appear before urban history shifts the scale dramatically to Kowloon Walled City.

s06e13.description: CRISPR gene editing, Van Gogh’s impasto, wedding-anniversary materials and the motorway hard shoulder all enter the ladder before engineering and geography combine at Egypt’s Aswan High Dam.
